founder_acceptance.rationale: Two review campaigns, the cap, ran on a high-risk package. Campaign 1 raised 2 blocking findings and 3 product decisions; the owner answered the decisions and all 75 findings were fixed (review-c1-disposition.md). Campaign 2 raised no blocking finding and no product decision; all 65 important/advisory findings were then fixed with none rejected (review-c2-disposition.md). The verdict stayed technical-changes-required only because no third campaign is allowed to confirm those fixes. The owner accepts the residual risk that a fix is incomplete, bounded by the compensating measures below. Panel caveat: all six lenses ran through a Claude-backed adapter (ADR-0025 exception chosen by the owner instead of the ADR-0024 Codex route), on one provider with three models (Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5). Opus 5.5 also authored the spec, so the panel is correlated and partly self-review; every lens is recorded as degraded and model-unverified.
compensating_measures: Every PR slice from tasks.md gets its own independent review and full CI before landing, per ADR-0008 and ADR-0023; ASK-class slices need the owner's recorded approval.
Each slice's PR description lists the review-c1/c2 dispositions it implements, so a reviewer can check that the planned fix actually landed in code.
/speckit-accept runs before release and maps every FR and SC to a named executable test with fresh Allure evidence; a reject verdict blocks the feature flag rollout.
The weekly_review flag stays OFF in production until the owner has completed the definition-of-done checks in intake.md on TestFlight and web.
If any slice changes spec.md, plan.md or a contract beyond the dispositions, the planning review is re-run for that change instead of relying on this acceptance.
